DEPARTMENT OF STATE 
Washington, D.C. 20520
BUREAU OF OCEANS AND INTERNATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL AND SCIENTIFIC AFFAIRS
November 18, 1974
Mr. T. O. Jones
Acting Assistant Director for
National and International Programs
National Science Foundation
Washington, D. C. 20550
Dear Mr. Jones:
In response to your letter of October 29 addressed to Mr. Bengels-dorf enclosing a draft statement on the Ross Ice Shelf Project, we have the following comment:
In our view, the statement glosses over the potential environmental impact of an oil spill should it occur as a result of drilling (pages 30 and 31). Oil slicks in polar waters are very slow to disperse, and it is misleading to state that "this pool of petroleum-soaked ice would eventually reach the front of the Ross Ice Shelf, be added to the marine environment and be dispersed in the same manner as oil slicks elsewhere." We suggest that the statement be amended to reflect more fully the magnitudes and hazards involved.
Yours truly.
Slator C. Blackiston, Jr
Office of Environmental Affairs
